original.question: Find the Maclaurin polynomials $p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3$ and the nth Maclaurin polynomial $p_n$ for $e^{x}$.
original.answer:
Every derivative of $e^x$ is $e^x$, so $f^{(k)}(0)=e^0=1$ for all $k$.
$p_0(x)=1$
$p_1(x)=1+x$
$p_2(x)=1+x+\dfrac{x^2}{2!}=1+x+\dfrac12x^2$
$p_3(x)=1+x+\dfrac{x^2}{2!}+\dfrac{x^3}{3!}=1+x+\dfrac12x^2+\dfrac16x^3$
$p_n(x)=1+x+\dfrac{x^2}{2!}+\cdots+\dfrac{x^n}{n!}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\dfrac{x^k}{k!}$
